Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.

This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a viral mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to find new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective as the virus evolves and acquires resistance.

The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.

This study uses integrated network analysis to explore how the traditional Chinese medicine Xiaojin Pill (XJP) might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks when co-administered with sorafenib. The work is largely computational/predictive, identifying candidate mechanisms and potential combination risks rather than providing experimental validation. It suggests XJP may have pharmacological potential as an adjunct to sorafenib, but the findings remain hypothesis-generating.

GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.

GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes for the many Golgi-associated proteins whose assemblies remain uncharacterized, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.

The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions of proteins rather than whole-sequence embeddings. This addresses the problem that whole-sequence representations can dilute catalytic residue and domain signals, while avoiding the need for accurate 3D structures. The approach aims to improve Enzyme Commission number prediction for protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction.

Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.

This study reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of thirteen benzimidazole derivatives as α-glucosidase inhibitors, identifying compounds 6 and 13 as the most potent with IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM, respectively—both more potent than the standard drug acarbose (IC50 = 139 μM). Structure-activity analysis highlighted a C-6 chlorine substituent and appropriate pendant aromatic ring substituents as key for activity, and computational studies indicated an uncompetitive mode of inhibition.

Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.

Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-provided distance constraints (e.g., from crosslinking or other experiments) into AlphaFold-Multimer-based protein complex structure prediction. It uses a multi-step protocol to guide assembly toward experimentally supported conformations, improving accuracy when standard prediction fails to correctly assemble complexes. The tool is aimed at cases where sparse distance data exist but are not automatically used by existing predictors.

Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.

This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational energetics of serine versus threonine at position 195 in thrombin, a key catalytic residue in trypsin-like serine proteases. The authors find that S195 and T195 occupy distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes, with S195 preferring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state, offering a molecular explanation for the strong evolutionary conservation of serine over threonine at this catalytic nucleophile position.

Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.

This preprint introduces three edge-aware graph attention network variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, differing in how edge features are incorporated during message passing. The authors show these models improve on a standard GAT and use the learned attention to derive communication networks that offer mechanistic interpretation of biophysical processes. The work aims to bridge predictive AI with interpretable biophysical insight.

Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.

This preprint reports cryo-EM structures of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) bound to G protein with either the natural ligand angiotensin II or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The two ligands adopt similar poses but trigger coordinated structural rearrangements that propagate from the ligand-binding pocket to the intracellular surface, revealing how biased signaling is encoded structurally. These structures provide a template for designing safer cardiovascular drugs that preferentially activate G protein rather than β-arrestin pathways.

AT1R-Selective Negative Allosteric Modulator Targeting the Epitope for Pathogenic Autoantibody Activation.

This preprint describes the development of a selective negative allosteric modulator (NAM) for the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) that targets the extracellular epitope recognized by pathogenic autoantibodies. Unlike conventional ARBs that block the orthosteric AngII binding site and thus inhibit both pathological and physiological signaling, this NAM aims to specifically prevent autoantibody-driven AT1R activation while sparing normal AngII signaling. The work addresses an unmet need in autoimmune cardiovascular and renal diseases where chronic AT1R activation is antibody-mediated.

From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.

This review argues that AI-driven protein design has moved beyond structure prediction to actively creating novel enzymes, using the vast uncharacterized microbial sequence space as both a source of starting points and a testing ground. It surveys three stages: mining microbial sequence space, generative design of new biocatalysts, and deployment in microbial expression hosts.
